title: Route Runtime, Security, and Extension
readerIntent: Define and operate a route through the governed request pipeline.
priorKnowledge: Know the controller/service operation and caller types.
owner: Owning route module and Nodics request pipeline
summary: The runtime checks API exposure, context, credential class, permissions, limits, and request shape before controller dispatch, then maps stable outcomes through response handlers.

sections.heading: Request flow
items: Match method and route and confirm its API-exposure category is enabled.
Apply HTTP headers, CORS, proxy, body-size, and rate guardrails.
Resolve enterprise, tenant, correlation, and module context.
Authenticate the permitted token class; authTokenTypes may restrict a route to service or other supported credentials before authorization.
Normalize request parameters, query, headers, and body.
Dispatch a thin controller to facade/service behavior.
Map success or error through the registered status and safe response contract.

sections.heading: Extension
items: Add business routes in the owning module under router definitions.
Use layered permissionConfig and apiExposure when values vary.
Version breaking API changes and regenerate OpenAPI.
Do not add hidden Express middleware, database calls, or business policy in routers/controllers.
Test public, human-authenticated, service-only, unauthorized, disabled-exposure, malformed, boundary, and regression behavior.
